notes: Flora of North America recognizes Euphorbia bicolor as a species.
Do not confuse the showy white structures with petals: the upper bracts are white-margined and the true inflorescence is a cyathium.

target_zone_range_leads.guardrail: Scout collects leads only; Deep Review must verify exact target-zone counties before PASS/FAIL/HOLD.
leads: Master Plant Pool has 7 personal wild observations.
UT's Hays County flora explicitly documents Euphorbia bicolor in north Hays County.
UT Wildflowers of Texas describes it as common in eastern, central, and north-central Texas.
FNA gives a native range including Texas and blackland/calcareous prairies.
BONAP Euphorbia county maps should be checked for exact target-zone county evidence.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Compare the upper leaf/bract shape and hairiness. Snow-on-the-prairie has long, narrow linear-to-narrowly-oblanceolate white-margined bracts and conspicuous hairiness on the plant.
diagnostic_traits: upper bracts linear to narrowly oblanceolate with conspicuous white margins
cyathia with 4–5 glands bearing white petal-like appendages

confusers.separator: E. bicolor has much narrower upper bracts and is hairy on the upper leaf surfaces/plant; E. marginata usually has broader elliptic bracts and upper leaf surfaces that are mostly glabrous.
